outcome_intro: See every client's Keeper 2FA coverage, weak and reused passwords, BreachWatch exposure, inactive users and seats in one run, then ask what changed since last quarter. Keeper Security + your AI reads through your own Commander Service Mode host and stores each run locally. It is read-only, and it has no path to a vault record.

instead_of_say.instead: Open the Keeper console for each managed company and note who still has 2FA off
instead_of_say.say: Which clients have users without 2FA, admins first?

instead_of_say.instead: Rebuild last quarter's password-health spreadsheet by hand and compare it to this one
instead_of_say.say: What changed in Keeper posture since the last run?

instead_of_say.instead: Search client by client to find which company a departing user belongs to
instead_of_say.say: Which client is jane@example.com in, and when did they last log in?

pain_points: Password health and 2FA are read per tenant, so a QBR across a book of clients means repeating the same look client by client. A 2026 review for MSPs describes the weak and reused password view as "per tenant".

Keeper's own reports do not answer "what changed since last quarter" across clients without someone keeping the earlier numbers; Keeper's MSP best practices recommend change and activity reports plus alerts, and advanced reporting is an add-on on some plans.

outcomes.question: How is every client doing on 2FA, weak passwords and BreachWatch?
Which clients have users without 2FA, admins first?
What changed since the last posture run, by client and by user?
Which invites went stale, and who is inactive or locked?
Which managed company does this user belong to?
How many seats does each client have allocated and active?

different_vs_wrappers: Most password-manager integrations, and an MCP server that only forwards each tool call, answer about one tenant now. This skill stores each cross-client posture run locally, so "what changed" and "who has no 2FA anywhere" are one offline query, and every command it can send is on a short fixed read-only allowlist it prints with keeper-cli allowlist.
different_vs_vendor: The Keeper Admin Console and MSP Console stay your place to change users, roles and seats; this skill adds cross-client posture history in the AI agent you already use, and complements the console rather than replacing it.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, so it needs the Keeper Security MCP server's token-protected HTTP mode hosted over HTTPS. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.

faqs.q: Is my Keeper Security data safe?
faqs.a: Your data stays on your machine and your own Service Mode host. Typed reads are printed and not saved; only posture report saves metrics and per-user facts to a local store. The skill cannot read a vault record, and a response shaped like record content is refused whole.

faqs.q: Can this read passwords from a client's vault?
faqs.a: No. It can send only the admin and MSP reports listed by keeper-cli allowlist, each with fixed read-only flags. Set the same list on your Service Mode key with service-create -c, so Service Mode refuses anything else too.

faqs.q: What do I need from Keeper?
faqs.a: Keeper Commander running in Service Mode on a host you control, over TLS (service-create with -crtf and -crtp), and its API key. The CLI refuses plain http on every host, localhost included. A private certificate is trusted with KEEPER_CA_CERT.

faqs.q: Do I need a Keeper MSP account?
faqs.a: The cross-client commands need one. An account that is not an MSP is reported as its own enterprise, one company in the same format.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

governance_summary: The skill reads Keeper admin and MSP reports: companies, seats, users, roles, teams, 2FA, password-health scores, BreachWatch summaries and audit events. It cannot change anything in Keeper and cannot read a vault record. The only things it writes are local: posture runs, learnings and profiles. Let an agent read freely, and keep a human on the credential commands.

posture report (reads Keeper, saves the run locally), teach, playbook amend, learnings forget, profile save, local-data purge
